population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
note: Three apoA-I infusions (MDCO-216, CER-001, CSL112) raised human efflux as animals predicted, yet none regressed plaque against placebo and CSL112 failed its outcome trial.
label: ACS (apoA-I infusion)

engagement.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
engagement.judgement: apoA-I Milano/DPPC (Esperion) is a sibling formulation of MDCO-216 (apoA-I Milano/POPC), so product_in_model false.
engagement.model: ApoE-/- mice infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid
engagement.note: A single apoA-I Milano dose nearly doubled plasma efflux capacity and raised serum free cholesterol in apoE-/- mice.
engagement.quote: One hour after injection, the plasma cholesterol efflux-promoting capacity was nearly 2-fold higher in recombinant apoA-I(m)-treated mice compared with saline and DPPC-treated mice (P<0.01).

engagement.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
engagement.model: Rabbits infused with CSL112 (plasma efflux PD)
engagement.note: CSL112 infusion into rabbits immediately raised ABCA1-dependent plasma efflux and unesterified cholesterol. Model first public after reconstituted HDL raised plasma efflux in patients (Patel 2009), so its comparisons are retrodictions.
engagement.quote: Infusion of CSL112 into rabbits caused a strong and immediate increase in the ATP binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1)-dependent efflux capacity of plasma, an increase in plasma unesterified cholesterol and rapid subsequent cholesterol esterification.

engagement.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Human phase 1 mobilization data appear only as a conference abstract (not admissible); not retrieved.
engagement.note: CER-001 transiently mobilized unesterified cholesterol into HDL in mice; no peer-reviewed human efflux or mobilization data found. Model first public after reconstituted HDL raised plasma efflux in patients (Patel 2009), so its comparisons are retrodictions.
engagement.quote: Following infusion of CER-001 (10mg/kg) in C57Bl/6J mice, we observed a transient increase in the mobilization of unesterified cholesterol in HDL particles containing recombinant human apoA-I.
engagement.reason: Human PD only in meeting abstracts

engagement.magnitude_basis: ABCA1-dependent plasma efflux capacity (human up to +630%)
engagement.population: Healthy volunteers (single and multiple ascending dose)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed). AEGIS-I (Gibson 2016, doi:10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.116.025687) confirmed the efflux rise in acute MI patients. Easton 2014 MAD paper (epub Oct 2013) not read.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (same sponsor, separate papers). Rabbit fold-change not in the abstract, so direction only.
engagement.model: Rabbits infused with CSL112 (plasma efflux PD)
engagement.note: In single and multiple ascending dose trials CSL112 raised ABCA1-dependent efflux up to 630%, dose-proportionally, as in rabbits. Retrodiction: reconstituted HDL had already raised plasma efflux capacity 40-60% in patients (Patel 2009, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2008.12.008) before this model was public in 2013, so the match is retro.
engagement.quote: Underlying this movement of cholesterol was an immediate and strong rise in the ability of plasma to promote cholesterol efflux from cells ex vivo.
engagement.reason: Human efflux rose as rabbits showed

engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma ABCA1-mediated efflux capacity after a single infusion
engagement.population: Healthy volunteers and stable coronary artery disease
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed); epub Dec 2015. Kempen 2016 (doi:10.1016/j.atherosclerosis.2016.10.042) adds a dose-dependent free-cholesterol rise. SAD trial registry not looked up.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: efflux capacity is the readout both papers share; healthy volunteers count. Fold-change scales differ (mouse total efflux vs human ABCA1 efflux), so direction only.
engagement.model: ApoE-/- mice infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid
engagement.note: A single MDCO-216 infusion in healthy volunteers and stable CAD patients profoundly raised ABCA1-mediated efflux, as in mice.
engagement.quote: Prominent and sustained increases in triglyceride, and decreases in HDL-C, endogenous ApoA-1 and ApoA-II occurred at doses >20 mg/kg and profound increases in ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux were observed.
engagement.reason: Human efflux rose as mice showed

engagement.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
engagement.judgement: Separate system from the same paper's rabbit infusions (draft track rabbit-csl112-efflux).
engagement.quote: In the presence of human plasma, CSL112 was significantly more potent than native HDL at enhancing cholesterol efflux from macrophages, and the efflux elevation was predominantly via the ABCA1 transporter.
engagement.note: CSL112 added to human plasma ex vivo raised macrophage cholesterol efflux, mainly via ABCA1. Model first public after reconstituted HDL raised plasma efflux in patients (Patel 2009), so its comparisons are retrodictions.
engagement.model: Human plasma and whole blood spiked with CSL112 ex vivo (macrophage efflux)

engagement.magnitude_basis: ABCA1-dependent plasma efflux capacity (human up to +630%)
engagement.population: Healthy volunteers (single and multiple ascending dose)
engagement.judgement: Paired by me; same sponsor, separate papers.
engagement.quote: Underlying this movement of cholesterol was an immediate and strong rise in the ability of plasma to promote cholesterol efflux from cells ex vivo.
engagement.note: CSL112 dosed to volunteers raised ABCA1-dependent plasma efflux up to 630%, as spiked plasma predicted. Retrodiction: reconstituted HDL had already raised plasma efflux capacity 40-60% in patients (Patel 2009, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2008.12.008) before this model was public in 2013, so the match is retro.
engagement.reason: Dosed-human efflux rose as ex vivo
engagement.model: Human plasma and whole blood spiked with CSL112 ex vivo (macrophage efflux)

engagement.judgement: Engagement counts any dosed humans; FHA patients are another disease. Paired by me with Tardy 2014 mouse mobilization.
engagement.note: Open-label: 20 CER-001 infusions (8 mg/kg) raised plasma-mediated efflux 44% in seven FHA patients, as mice showed cholesterol mobilization. Retrodiction: rHDL had raised human efflux in 2009 (Patel 2009).
engagement.quote: CER-001 induced a 44% relative increase (P = 0.018) in in vitro cellular cholesterol efflux with a trend toward increased FSE (P = 0.068).

dose.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
dose.model: ApoE-/- mice infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid
dose.note: Mouse regimens (40 mg/kg every other day) stated no human exposure target or margin; ETC-216 and MDCO-216 doses were set in humans.
dose.quote: Treated mice received 18 injections of either 40 mg/kg apo A-I(Milano)/PC (n=15) or PC only (n=5) intravenously every other day from 20 weeks until death at 25 weeks.

dose.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
dose.model: Rabbits infused with CSL112 (plasma efflux PD)
dose.note: Rabbit PK was described as favourable but no human exposure target or margin was stated; human doses came from ascending-dose trials.
dose.quote: CSL112 is a disc-shaped particle that strongly elevates cholesterol esterification and shows good pharmacokinetics in rabbits.

dose.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
dose.judgement: Tardy 2015 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0137584) later reported inverse dose dependence in apoE-/- mice, after CHI-SQUARE; a retrodiction not scored here because only its title was read.
dose.note: Mouse regression at 10 mg/kg every 2 days stated no human target; CHI-SQUARE tested 3-12 mg/kg weekly.
dose.quote: In a familial hypercholesterolemia mouse model (LDL-receptor deficient mice), the infusion of CER-001 caused 17% and 32% reductions in plaque size, 17% and 23% reductions in lipid content after 5 and 10 doses given every 2 days, respectively.

dose.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
dose.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy for the pre-phase-1 toxicology (date and species not in the abstract; full text fetch failed).
dose.quote: We report the first phase I study results with CER-001 in humans, starting at 0.25 mg/kg, which is 1/80th of the safe dose (20 mg/kg) established in 4-week multiple-dose animal studies dosed every second day.
dose.note: Animal repeat-dose studies set 20 mg/kg as safe, above the 10 mg/kg mouse regression dose; first-in-human started at 1/80th.
dose.model: CER-001 4-week repeat-dose animal toxicology (every second day)

dose.magnitude_basis: animal safe dose 20 mg/kg vs human single doses tolerated to 45 mg/kg
dose.judgement: The animal safe dose exceeded the mouse effective dose (a stated margin); volunteers were dosed past both without toxicity. Source sets animal and human data side by side.
dose.quote: All CER-001 doses (0.25-45 mg/kg) were safe and well tolerated, with an adverse event profile similar to placebo.
dose.note: Single CER-001 doses to 45 mg/kg were tolerated in volunteers, so the animal margin over effective doses held.
dose.model: CER-001 4-week repeat-dose animal toxicology (every second day)

efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.model: ApoE-/- mice infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid
efficacy.note: apoA-I Milano/phospholipid halted aortic plaque progression and cut plaque lipid and macrophages in apoE-/- mice.
efficacy.quote: Recombinant A-I(Milano)/PC prevented progression of aortic atherosclerosis and reduced lipid and macrophage content of plaques in apo E-deficient mice despite severe hypercholesterolemia.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: percent atheroma volume change on IVUS (-1.06% vs baseline)
efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in the pooled ETC-216 arms (P=.02); the comparison with placebo was not significant.
efficacy.judgement: ETC-216 counted as the member MDCO-216 (same apoA-I Milano/POPC complex, new manufacturing process). Same, partial: the prespecified within-group primary was met but not superiority over placebo. Paired by me; the trial only cites animal regression.
efficacy.model: ApoE-/- mice infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid
efficacy.note: ETC-216, the predecessor formulation of MDCO-216, regressed coronary atheroma volume after five weekly infusions in 47 ACS patients. ETC-216 is scored as MDCO-216, the same apoA-I Milano/POPC complex made by a newer process.
efficacy.quote: A recombinant ApoA-I Milano/phospholipid complex (ETC-216) administered intravenously for 5 doses at weekly intervals produced significant regression of coronary atherosclerosis as measured by IVUS.

efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.note: CER-001 reduced plaque size 17-32% and macrophage content in LDLr-/- mice after 5-10 doses.
efficacy.quote: These data demonstrate that CER-001 rapidly enhances reverse lipid transport in the mouse, reducing vascular inflammation and promoting regression of diet-induced atherosclerosis in LDLr(-/-) mice upon a short-term multiple dose treatment.

efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. No CSL112 plaque-regression animal study before AEGIS-II was found.
efficacy.judgement: AEGIS-II (the class's phase 3) failed its MACE primary, but the only CSL112 model stated an efflux rise, not regression or events, so efficacy stays untested rather than contra.
efficacy.model: Rabbits infused with CSL112 (plasma efflux PD)
efficacy.note: The rabbit work measured efflux only, no plaque or events; AEGIS-II's null MACE result tests no model prediction. The member apolipoprotein a-i is CSL112 here; CSL111 (ERASE) not scored.
efficacy.quote: Preferential elevation of ABCA1-dependent efflux may target atherosclerotic plaque for cholesterol removal and this property makes CSL112 a promising candidate therapy for acute coronary syndrome.

patient_trials.quote: There was no significant difference between the groups in the risk of a primary end-point event at 90 days of follow-up (439 patients [4.8%] in the CSL112 group vs. 472 patients [5.2%] in the placebo group

efficacy.magnitude_basis: nominal change in total atheroma volume, 12 mg/kg vs placebo (P=0.81)
efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed, PMC4258222). NCT01201837 has no posted results. The mouse paper appeared Nov 2013 while the trial was running, before its results.
efficacy.judgement: Scored prospective: the mouse data were generated before CHI-SQUARE read out. CARAT (2018) repeated the null at 3 mg/kg in high-burden ACS patients, listed as a patient trial.
efficacy.note: CHI-SQUARE: six weekly CER-001 infusions (3-12 mg/kg) did not reduce coronary atheroma on IVUS in 507 ACS patients.
efficacy.quote: CER-001 infusions did not reduce coronary atherosclerosis on IVUS and QCA when compared with placebo.

patient_trials.quote: The primary efficacy measure, PAV, decreased 0.41% with placebo (P = .005 compared with baseline), but not with CER-001 (-0.09%; P = .67 compared with baseline; between group differences, 0.32%; P = .15).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: placebo-adjusted change in percent atheroma volume (+0.73%, P=.07)
efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PubMed, PMC6233637). Year from NCT02678923 results posting 2017-07-13; paper July 2018.
efficacy.judgement: Contra on the mouse track: the regression the mice predicted did not appear against placebo with background statins. One member's contra outranks the earlier ETC-216 same.
efficacy.model: ApoE-/- mice infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid
efficacy.note: MILANO-PILOT: five weekly MDCO-216 infusions on statins did not regress coronary atheroma more than placebo in 122 ACS patients. Dated 2016: results were presented at AHA and in a Cleveland Clinic release on 2016-11-15 (newsroom.clevelandclinic.org/2016/11/15), before the 2017 registry posting. Background statins in both arms are not a combination partner, so the trial scores as contra.
efficacy.quote: Among patients with an acute coronary syndrome, infusing MDCO-216 did not produce an incremental plaque regression in the setting of contemporary statin therapy.

efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.judgement: AIM-PL formulation not stated as ETC-216 in the abstract, so product_in_model false.
efficacy.quote: Infusion of AIM-PL at the 2 highest doses caused reduction of right carotid artery plaque area by the end a 90-minute infusion as assessed by IVUS analysis.
efficacy.note: A single apoA-I Milano/phospholipid infusion regressed rabbit carotid plaque on IVUS within 90 minutes.
efficacy.short: Rabbit carotid plaque regressed on IVUS
efficacy.model: Rabbits with perivascular-injury carotid plaques infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid (IVUS, MRI)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: percent atheroma volume change on IVUS (-1.06% vs baseline, pooled ETC-216)
efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: both use IVUS plaque volume. ETC-216 counted as member MDCO-216, as in the draft. Same, partial: within-group primary met, not superiority over placebo.
efficacy.quote: A recombinant ApoA-I Milano/phospholipid complex (ETC-216) administered intravenously for 5 doses at weekly intervals produced significant regression of coronary atherosclerosis as measured by IVUS.
efficacy.note: ETC-216 regressed coronary atheroma within-group after five weekly infusions in 47 ACS patients, as rabbit IVUS showed. ETC-216 is scored as MDCO-216, the same apoA-I Milano/POPC complex made by a newer process.
efficacy.model: Rabbits with perivascular-injury carotid plaques infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid (IVUS, MRI)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: placebo-adjusted change in percent atheroma volume (+0.73%, P=.07)
efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year from NCT02678923 results posting 2017-07-13 (draft's dating); results were presented and the program stopped 2016-11-15.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. Parolini 2008 (ETC-216 5-150 mg/kg x5) is the track's prospective prediction for MILANO-PILOT (20 mg/kg x5): reduced progression at low doses, regression at high. Statin background never tested in rabbits (rule question raised by checker).
efficacy.quote: Among patients with an acute coronary syndrome, infusing MDCO-216 did not produce an incremental plaque regression in the setting of contemporary statin therapy.
efficacy.note: Rabbits given repeated ETC-216 showed dose-related less progression or regression; MILANO-PILOT's MDCO-216 gave no regression versus placebo. Dated 2016: results were presented at AHA and in a Cleveland Clinic release on 2016-11-15 (newsroom.clevelandclinic.org/2016/11/15), before the 2017 registry posting. Background statins in both arms are not a combination partner, so the trial scores as contra.
efficacy.reason: Rabbit regression not seen in patients
efficacy.model: Rabbits with perivascular-injury carotid plaques infused with apoA-I Milano/phospholipid (IVUS, MRI)

efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.judgement: Natural variant, not the drug: product_in_model false. Treated as a human genetic model predicting that apoA-I Milano is anti-atherogenic.
efficacy.quote: Despite severe HA, carriers of the apoA-I(M) mutant do not show structural changes in the arteries and heart
efficacy.note: Twenty-one apoA-I Milano carriers had normal carotid IMT despite very low HDL, the rationale for infusing the variant.
efficacy.model: ApoA-I Milano carriers (Limone sul Garda kindred), carotid IMT

efficacy.magnitude_basis: percent atheroma volume change on IVUS (-1.06% vs baseline, pooled ETC-216)
efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me; the carrier phenotype is lifelong exposure, the trial five infusions, so direction only. Same, partial as on the draft's mouse track.
efficacy.quote: A recombinant ApoA-I Milano/phospholipid complex (ETC-216) administered intravenously for 5 doses at weekly intervals produced significant regression of coronary atherosclerosis as measured by IVUS.
efficacy.note: ETC-216 (recombinant apoA-I Milano) regressed coronary atheroma within-group in 47 ACS patients, as carriers' protection implied. ETC-216 is scored as MDCO-216, the same apoA-I Milano/POPC complex made by a newer process.
efficacy.model: ApoA-I Milano carriers (Limone sul Garda kindred), carotid IMT

efficacy.magnitude_basis: placebo-adjusted change in percent atheroma volume (+0.73%, P=.07)
efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year from NCT02678923 results posting 2017-07-13 (draft's dating); results were presented and the program stopped 2016-11-15.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. Kallend 2016 cites the carriers as the class's basis; contra because the infused variant gave no anti-atherosclerotic effect.
efficacy.quote: Among patients with an acute coronary syndrome, infusing MDCO-216 did not produce an incremental plaque regression in the setting of contemporary statin therapy.

efficacy.reason: Carrier protection not reproduced by infusion
efficacy.model: ApoA-I Milano carriers (Limone sul Garda kindred), carotid IMT

efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.quote: Common genetic variation in APOA1 associated with increased apoA-I and HDL cholesterol levels did not associate with decreased risk of IHD or MI.
efficacy.note: Genetically higher apoA-I (up to 6.6%) did not lower ischaemic heart disease or MI risk, predicting no benefit from raising apoA-I.
efficacy.short: Genetically higher apoA-I, no IHD benefit
efficacy.model: Common APOA1 variants raising apoA-I (Copenhagen City Heart Study), IHD/MI risk

efficacy.magnitude_basis: MACE risk: genetic null vs AEGIS-II 4.8% vs 5.2% at 90 days (ns)
efficacy.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; quote as the checker verified in the draft's patient_trials. Lifelong small apoA-I rise versus acute large infusion limits the analogy.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me. The genetics spoke to IHD/MI events, so the IVUS trials (CHI-SQUARE 2014, MILANO-PILOT, CARAT) do not test it; AEGIS-II is the first events trial of a member.
efficacy.quote: There was no significant difference between the groups in the risk of a primary end-point event at 90 days of follow-up (439 patients [4.8%] in the CSL112 group vs. 472 patients [5.2%] in the placebo group
efficacy.note: AEGIS-II: four CSL112 infusions did not reduce 90-day MACE in 18,219 AMI patients, as the APOA1 genetics predicted.

efficacy.model: Common APOA1 variants raising apoA-I (Copenhagen City Heart Study), IHD/MI risk

safety.population: Unselected (recent acute coronary syndrome or acute MI)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Model year is a proxy (Diditchenko 2013).
safety.note: CSL112 toxicology is not public; AEGIS-I met its hepatic and renal safety margins and AEGIS-II later found more hypersensitivity.
safety.quote: Among patients with acute myocardial infarction, 4 weekly infusions of CSL112 are feasible, well tolerated, and not associated with any significant alterations in liver or kidney function or other safety concern.

safety.magnitude_basis: IL-6 ratio over background (MDCO-216 ~1 vs ETC-216 4-16)
safety.population: Healthy volunteers and stable CAD (ex vivo arm also acute CAD)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMC5591804). imported_from MONDO:0005010 (coronary artery disorder, checked in OLS) stands for stable CAD.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the in vivo SAD data (Kallend 2016) were public before the ex vivo assay was reported. Imported from stable CAD and healthy volunteers, not ACS.
safety.note: Ex vivo, MDCO-216 provoked no IL-6 or TNF in donor blood, matching no inflammation in dosed volunteers and stable CAD patients.
safety.short: No cytokines ex vivo or in vivo
safety.quote: MDCO-216 did not induce adverse immunostimulation in HV and sCAD patients, in contrast to ETC-216.
